<header class="ws-head"><span class="ws-kicker">Day 1 · 11:40–12:30 · Technical module 2 · serves M3</span><h2>Offline data capture<span class="ws-badge">Draft</span></h2><p class="ws-carries">How does a form on a health worker's phone become a patient record, with no signal?</p></header>
<h3>Sessions</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Lab</span><span class="ws-sheet">11:40–12:30 · 50 min</span></span><b>Lab 1: Offline data capture</b><p>The stack is already running on Heropa. Open a questionnaire in the form editor, change it, and watch the change appear in the OHS Player in your browser. Then add a validation rule or a skip rule. If time allows, see how the answers turn into FHIR resources. Optional: a QR code for the gallery app, to try the same forms on iOS or Android.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Fikri · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>Simon Njoroge</p></div></div>
<h3>By the end you can</h3><ul><li>Edit a FHIR Questionnaire and see the result straight away</li><li>Add a validation or skip rule</li><li>Describe how captured answers become patient records</li></ul>
<h3>Where it meets the journey</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2a/">J2a</a><b>A health worker finds the baby — and reads his cards</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>The CHW app decodes the paper cards (read-unverified) and fills the form from them, without checking signatures.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>Which data elements can the form take from a scanned card, and how does it mark them as reported, not verified?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><b>Registered at home, and referred</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>The household registration Questionnaire; answers become Patient, Group (household) and reported Immunization, queued offline.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>Which validation or skip rule stops a duplicate child being registered in the same household?</p></div></div>
<h3>Technical questions for the room</h3><ul class="ws-qs"><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2a/">J2a</a><span>Which data elements can the form take from a scanned card, and how does it mark them as reported, not verified?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><span>Which validation or skip rule stops a duplicate child being registered in the same household?</span></li></ul>
<h3>Terms at those steps</h3><div class="ws-terms"><a href="glossary.html#term-point-of-service-application" title="Point-of-service applications are end-user application components (IT systems or software tools) used by individuals directly engaged in healthcare—such as clinicians, community health workers, and patients—that enable interaction with the broader healthcare ecosystem.">Point-of-Service Applications</a><a href="glossary.html#term-verifiable-credential" title="A digitally signed statement, such as a vaccination record, that anyone can check is genuine and unaltered.">Verifiable credential</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-signature" title="A cryptographic seal made with the issuer's private key. Verifiers check it with the matching public key.">Digital signature</a><a href="glossary.html#term-core-data-set" title="The elements a country agrees to record for a use case, each mapped to standard codes. Also called a minimum data set.">Core data set</a><a href="glossary.html#term-client-registry" title="The Client Registry is the national authoritative source of health-specific person identity.
